newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Asiatrust says IPO foreign tranche sold out.
newsitem.headline: Manila Asiatrust says IPO foreign tranche sold out.

text.p: Philippine private development bank Asiatrust Bank said on Monday the foreign tranche of its initial public offering was oversubscribed.
"Definitely it's more than two times oversubscribed so our problem now is trying to allocate enough for everyone," Dionisio C. Ong, Asiatrust Bank president told Reuters.
The offering, the first for a private development bank in the country, is expected to generate 750 million pesos.
The offering for the entire 18,818,000 shares, which represent 27.14 percent of the bank's outstanding stock, started Sept 3 and will end on Sept 12.
Foreigners were offered 7,527,200 shares while the remaining 11,290,800 shares is for local investors.
The shares are being offered at 39.88 pesos.
The multilateral lending agency, Asian Development Bank, is a shareholder in Asiatrust.
